Period of internship: Fall 2026

As a student you are probably looking for the perfect Internship. An internship, where you can utilize what you have learned throughout your studies and at the same time learn much more about what it is like to work in a company. If so, we definitely have the right fit for you at Eurowind Energy A/S!

We have collaborated with many students, who have helped us with new and exciting solutions, and we are currently looking for new students to do the same. In fact, we have employed several of our interns after their graduation, and we hope that we can keep doing so.

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 different countries across Europe, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation’s “Power Major”. Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for innovative ideas and the latest knowledge

You will be part of the department Photovoltaic Asset Management where you will participate in the daily operation and development of solar parks. In PVAM, you will work within some of our main areas, where your tasks will be a combination of office and field work.

Solar (PV)

Ordinary maintenance, troubleshooting & extraordinary maintenance

• Our main purpose is to ensure a high uptime for our PV-plants. Most of the incidents causing downtime are preventable with preventative maintenance, which we perform. Some incidents are caused by weather incidents or similar, where our job is to troubleshoot; access the damage, find the cause of failure and ensure that the necessary repairs are carried out. This may include electrical measurements, replacing components and more. This includes electrical measurements, replacing components and more.

Warranty claims

• Based on the cause of failure we are responsible for submitting warranty claims and coordination of warranty repairs; spare parts, work crew etc.

SCADA monitoring & data analyzis

• All our parks are monitored online, where we have SCADA systems to monitor asset performance and alarms to notify us of any irregularities.

• Using data, we can identify the root cause of most faults and implement procedures to prevent future accidents.

Commissioning & quality assesment

• When we build new parks, our crew is on site to follow the building progress and inspect the work done.

Design & optimization

• Our department is a knowledge center, where our input is valuable for the design/redesign of existing and future parks. We build power plants with ambitions of running those assets for up to 30 years. Every plant we build, we get more experience and realize what could be done better in the future. Furthermore, we look into optimizing the plants for lower losses and easier maintenance.

Technical & commercial support

• We provide support for our other departments; investors, battery, wind and foreign PV departments. Furthermore, we provide training in the above for our PV departments worldwide.

Project engineering and modelling of new facilities. In the future, we would like to have a PV test facility at our HQ, which we need to design.

Hybrid parks

• Co-operation of hybrid parks with integration of wind turbines, PV and batteries. Here, both grid connections and internal connections between the energy plants can be examined.

• Predictions and calculations of production with the primary aim of production planning and regulation

About you

Maybe you are studying to become Marine Engineer, electrical Engineer or similar, but most importantly – you want to contribute with your knowledge and your excellent questions when we have our heads up to our eyes in numbers, developing components or are visiting one of our wind or solar parks. At Eurowind, we value flexibility and work-life-balance highly.

We offer you an exciting internship in a fast-growing company and an attractive industry.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Did we capture your attention?

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below.

Should you have any questions before applying, please feel free to contact Technical Operation Manager Sif Þorsteinsdóttir Hesselvig at sihe@ewe.dk

The internship is unpaid.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy on our website or LinkedIn.

Our employees stand out from others thanks to their ability to supply innovative solutions to our customers. They can do this because they know the industry and are passionate about continuously developing and expanding their knowledge. We support these high standards through teamwork, mutual respect and a working culture based on trust that fosters stability and security for all of our employees. Our common goal is to implement outstanding and innovative projects worldwide.

WHAT BENEFITS DO WE OFFER?

• 
We offer exciting opportunities in an internationally operating family-owned company with locations in more than 70 countries – including the opportunity to temporarily work from one of our international locations as part of our Flex Abroad Program.

• 
During our immersive onboarding program in, you will receive an extensive overview of BEUMER Group, our history, and our vision for the future, whilst also getting to know your new colleagues.

Do you want to shape how we manage the financial performance of complex portfolio of EPC and service projects? Are you a strong people leader and trusted business partner, who can challenge senior stakeholders and set direction while being close to the details to know what is really going on? 

In Semco Renewables we are delivering complex EPC and service projects within the wind energy sector. With a growing project portfolio, strong project controlling is essential to ensure transparency, sound decision-making, and strong financial performance. Thus, we are looking for you who can lead and develop our Project Controlling while acting as business partner to project leadership and senior management. You will have the opportunity to shape how we work with project financials, forecasting, risk management, governance, and performance across the organization. 

Your position

You will head up our Project Controlling function and lead a team of 10 colleagues divided into Project Controllers and Senior Project Controllers supporting our EPC and service projects. The Project Controllers are placed on locations in Denmark, Germany and Poland.

At Semco Maritime safety is a core value, and in this role, you will contribute to maintaining and promoting a strong safety culture while delivering innovative solutions. Above all, your work will make a real change for the global energy sector. 

Your place of work will be at our Global HQ located in Esbjerg, the hub of the Danish energy industry, right on the waterfront – views do not get any better than this. The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel approximately 30 days per year.  

“We are looking for a Senior Manager who can bring direction and structure to our Project Controlling function while remaining close to the business. Someone who can challenge us strategically, but who is also willing to get into the details when the situation requires it. Strong project controlling is not only about reporting numbers – it is about understanding what drives the numbers and using that insight to improve our projects and business” Claus Erdmann, VP Finance

Your tasks & responsibilities

As Senior Manager, you will have overall responsibility for ensuring that the financial performance of our project portfolio is transparent, well understood, and proactively managed. You will work closely with Project Directors, Project Managers and the Finance organization, providing financial insight and challenging decisions where needed. Further, you will be a close sparring partner to the VP Finance on project portfolio performance, risks, opportunities, lessons learned and strategic decisions. Thus, you will need to be comfortable moving between the strategic perspective and the operational details – from discussing portfolio performance and governance to diving into the numbers of an individual project when required. 

Your tasks will include but are not limited to: 

• Leading and developing the Project Controlling function ensuring strong performance, clear standards, and continuous competence development.
• Ensuring transparent and reliable financial management of the project portfolio, including revenue, margin, cash flow, forecast, and risks.
• Driving robust forecasting and Estimate-to-Complete processes, ensuring early identification and follow-up on deviations, risks, and opportunities.
• Acting as a trusted financial sparring partner to VP and project leadership, supporting sound commercial and strategic decisions.
• Driving strong project governance and continuous improvement while remaining close to the operational details when needed.

Your profile & qualifications

To succeed in this role, you need to be a strong leader, a trusted business partner, and an experienced project finance professional. You are comfortable challenging senior stakeholders and setting direction, while staying close enough to the operation to understand the details when it matters. You bring structure to complexity, turn financial insight into action, and create clarity for both your team and the wider business.

You will be a part of a team that prioritizes time and details on point and a flexible working environment. We are sociable, helpful, and open to input, as well as dedicated, executory, and structured in our work, with respect for the agility that is a natural part of our core task. We want the same from you.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

• Strong leadership experience and a proven ability to lead, develop, and challenge experienced financial professionals.
• Extensive experience with project controlling/project finance and a strong understanding of project economics, including margin, cash flow, forecasting, and Estimate-to-Complete.
• Strong business partnering skills and the confidence to challenge and advise Project Directors, senior management, and other key stakeholders.
• The ability to move between strategy and operations – seeing the bigger picture while being willing and able to dive into the details when needed.
• Experience from a complex, project-oriented environment, preferably within EPC, service, offshore, wind, energy, infrastructure, or engineering.
• A structured and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to turn complexity into clear processes, standards, and actionable insights.
• Strong communication skills and fluency in English, with the ability to communicate financial matters clearly to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.

Welcome to Semco Maritime 

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape. 

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in. 

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future. 

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too.  

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.   

Care to join the movement? 

Change. With us. 

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

Do you have a strong technical mindset and a passion for structure, quality, and well-prepared offshore execution? Do you want to play a key role in ensuring that service campaigns are executed safely, efficiently, and with the highest documentation standards? Then you might be our new Project Engineer within Balance of Plant Support at Semco Maritime.
 
Your position

As our new Project Engineer, you will be a vital part of the Balance of Plant Support team, where your primary responsibility will be to ensure the technical preparation and documentation required for safe and efficient offshore execution.

You will work closely with Project Managers, Site Managers, HSE, and engineering disciplines to ensure that all documentation — including RAMS, checklists, and execution plans — is complete, accurate, and aligned with project and client requirements. In this role, you will be at the forefront of ensuring documentation excellence and quality across our service projects.

At Semco Maritime, safety is a core value, and through your work you will actively contribute to maintaining and strengthening our safety culture by ensuring that offshore activities are thoroughly prepared and documented.

Your place of work will be at either Global HQ in Esbjerg, in Copenhagen, in Aarhus, in Hamburg or in Emden in Germany, with occasional travel related to service campaigns. The position is full-time.
 
“High-quality technical preparation is the foundation for safe offshore execution. In this role, you will make a direct impact on how our projects are prepared and delivered.”  - Senior Manager, BoP Support, Michael Andersen
 
Your tasks & responsibilities

As Project Engineer within BoP support, you will support the planning and execution of service activities through structured and high-quality documentation.
Your key tasks will include:

• Preparing and maintaining project documentation for offshore service activities
• Developing RAMS, work descriptions, and execution plans in close collaboration with project teams
• Creating and maintaining offshore checklists and readiness documentation
• Ensuring documentation complies with internal standards, client requirements, and applicable regulations
• Supporting Project Leaders and Site Managers with documentation reviews and updates
• Ensuring high-quality reporting before, during, and after offshore execution
• Contributing to continuous improvement of documentation standards, templates, and processes
• Supporting tender activities by providing technical input, developing execution concepts, and contributing to scope, methodology, and resource planning
 Your profile & qualifications

We are looking for a structured and detail-oriented Project Engineer who takes ownership of quality and thrives in a collaborative project environment.

To succeed in this role, you likely have:

• A relevant technical education, for example within marine, mechanical, electrical, offshore, or a similar engineering discipline
• Experience in project engineering, service operations, or offshore execution (advantageous)
• A good understanding of the requirements associated with offshore or industrial project execution
• Experience working with RAMS, work packs, Service Reporting or other execution documentation
• A high focus on quality, structure, and accuracy
• Strong communication skills in English. German is considered an advantage
• A proactive and solution-oriented mindset

Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too.

Care to join the movement?

Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Do you want to take technical ownership of the communication systems that help keep offshore wind farms safe, connected and operational? We’re looking for a Senior Telecom Engineer to develop, support and improve mission-critical telecommunications throughout the lifecycle of our operational and future offshore wind portfolio.

Telecommunications are critical to the safe and reliable operation of an offshore wind farm. In this senior engineering role, you will take technical responsibility for communication systems from early design and construction through commissioning, operations, maintenance and lifecycle replacement.

You will join our Digital Infrastructure & Connectivity organisation and work with a broad range of telecommunications technologies, with particular focus on mission-critical radio and offshore communication systems. These include TETRA, DMR, VHF/UHF radio, microwave and line-of-sight communications, AIS, ADS-B, Iridium and Starlink.

The role combines hands-on engineering, operational support, technical design, troubleshooting, stakeholder management and continuous improvement. Importantly, our involvement does not end when a project is commissioned. The Telecom team continues to support the systems it designs throughout their operational lifecycle.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Y****our role / what will you do?

You will take technical ownership of operational telecommunications infrastructure across the offshore wind portfolio and help ensure that communication systems remain secure, resilient, maintainable and available throughout the lifetime of our wind farms. You will support projects from tender and early engineering through construction, commissioning and transition into Operations & Maintenance, while also troubleshooting and improving systems already in operation. Working closely with operational stakeholders, project teams, suppliers and internal engineering disciplines, you will translate operational needs into robust technical solutions, guide complex engineering decisions and develop standardised concepts for future wind farms.

This is an operational engineering position as well as a project engineering role. You will develop a strong understanding of the workflows within the Marine Communications Center and Surveillance Center, including how telecommunications support normal wind-farm operations and emergency situations. You should therefore be comfortable working methodically under operational pressure, coordinating several technical contributors and following critical issues through to resolution. The position includes participation in a 24/7 on-call duty arrangement.

Your tasks and responsibilities:

• Take technical ownership of operational telecommunications infrastructure across the offshore wind portfolio.

• Design, implement, commission, operate and maintain mission-critical radio and telecommunications solutions.

• Support TETRA, DMR, VHF/UHF, microwave and line-of-sight, AIS, ADS-B, Iridium and satellite-based communication systems, including Starlink.

• Support wind-farm projects from tender and early engineering through construction, commissioning and transition into Operations & Maintenance.

• Perform and review site surveys, coverage calculations, technical designs, specifications, drawings, documentation, contractual requirements and engineering recommendations.

• Provide technical support for telecommunications used by wind-farm operations, marine coordination and surveillance functions, including emergency communication arrangements.

• Support marine coordination systems and integrate telecommunications equipment and services into infrastructure monitoring solutions.

• Monitor, troubleshoot and optimise existing telecommunications systems, including incidents and complex technical problems affecting operational services.

• Develop new telecommunications concepts and standardised technical solutions for future wind farms.

• Ensure systems are operated in accordance with applicable IT and OT security requirements.

• Produce and maintain engineering documentation, configurations and operational procedures.

• Support lifecycle planning, upgrades and replacement of ageing or obsolete telecommunications infrastructure.

• Work with suppliers, contractors, field teams, project organisations and internal engineering teams to ensure solutions meet technical and operational requirements.

• Ensure engineering activities are appropriately recorded and maintained through the Telecom support process and in JIRA.

• Identify opportunities to improve Telecom and Infrastructure processes and ways of working, and share technical knowledge with engineers and colleagues.

Your profile / who are you?

You are an experienced telecommunications engineer who combines strong technical judgement with a hands-on and structured approach to operational engineering. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex communication systems and following technical problems through to resolution, including when priorities change or operational pressure is high. You communicate clearly with engineers, operational teams, project organisations, management, suppliers and external partners, and you are confident challenging technical solutions while proposing practical alternatives. You value high-quality documentation and configuration management, work independently while contributing actively to the team, and willingly share knowledge to support the development of colleagues.

You do not need to be an expert in every technology from the first day. We value broad technical curiosity and expect our engineers to continue developing their knowledge as technologies and operational requirements evolve.

Next to this you bring:

• A degree or equivalent technical qualification in Telecommunications, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Network Engineering or a related discipline.

• Several years of professional experience in telecommunications, radio communications or critical infrastructure, with the ability to take technical responsibility for complex operational systems.

• Strong knowledge of radio communications and RF principles, including antennas, feeders, coverage, interference and radio-system troubleshooting.

• Experience with mission-critical radio systems, preferably TETRA and/or DMR.

• Knowledge of IPv4 networking, routing and multicast, together with experience integrating telecommunications systems into IP networks.

• An understanding of microwave or line-of-sight communication systems and basic knowledge of fibre-optic infrastructure.

• Experience supporting operational or business-critical telecommunications systems.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

Experience that would be valuable

• Experience from offshore wind, energy, utilities, maritime communications, OT/SCADA, emergency services, defence or another critical-infrastructure environment.

• Experience with AIS, ADS-B, Iridium, Starlink, VHF marine radio or other satellite communications.

• Experience supporting offshore operations, marine coordination or surveillance functions.

Travel and offshore work

The role involves engagement with Vattenfall sites and project locations. You should expect approximately 20 days of travel per year, although additional travel may be required during your initial onboarding period. During the first six months, travel may occasionally be required as frequently as every other week, depending on operational and training needs. Following onboarding, regular engagement with colleagues and stakeholders in Kolding and Esbjerg may also be required.

You must be able to obtain and maintain the appropriate offshore safety and medical qualifications required to access Vattenfall’s offshore assets, including relevant GWO and HUET training where applicable.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location  Kolding Denmark, Amsterdam, Netherlands

Additional Information

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can really find your element with us. We’ll also provide you with all the learning and development you need to expand your horizons.

We strive to be the best place to work in the industry with highly competitive pay and conditions and an open, supportive culture. A commitment to a healthy work-life balance aims to ensure everyone plays to their strengths, whatever their background and experiences.

You will be part of a growing team of 1,700+ colleagues from 50+ nationalities where our positive approach to diversity is reflected in the fact that more than a quarter of staff are women.

More Information

For more information about the position you are welcome to contact hiring manager Alin George Raducu, alingeorge.raducu@vattenfall.com.  For more information about the recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Christian Pathuel, christian.pathuel@vattenfall.com.

We welcome your application in English no later than 06.12.2026. We kindly request that you do not send applications by any means other than via our website.

At Vattenfall we are convinced that diversity contributes to building a more profitable and attractive company and we strive to be a good role model regarding diversity. Vattenfall works actively for all employees to have the same opportunities and rights regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, transgender identity or expression, religion or other belief, disability or sexual orientation. Click here for further information.

The security of Vattenfall and its employees is essential. For that reason, a pre-employment screening will be part of your recruitment process. The screening is based on the role you will fulfill within Vattenfall and will be performed by a third party, DISA Global Solutions AB.

Since Vattenfall is a part of the Swedish critical infrastructure, many of our services are security classed. If this position is security classified the final candidates might be subject to a security vetting process, according to Swedish legislation.

We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.occupation: Removing micropollutants and oxidation products by biofilm reactors (Project Optimise)
jobs.description:
The project will focus on developing and testing innovative bioreactors for ozonation post treatment (especially for removal of ozonation products) for wastewater treatment. The system will be developed in labscale but its relevance will be tested by analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in a small catchment receiving ozonated wastewater. Some samples will be analysed by partners by means of biosensing. Some sampling for micropollutants and ozonation products in recipients is part of optimize.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a 22 months position from 1st April 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description

 * Develop biofilm reactors for ozonation post treatment of wastewater
 * Analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in wastewater 
 * Analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in recipient
 * Documentation, reporting and publishing

Applicants must hold a PhD in environmental engineering, environmental chemistry, environmental science or similar.

Experiences in i)biofilm engineering and ii)biofilm reactors, iii)quantitation of organic micropollutants by means of HPLC-MS/MS and/or HPLC-HR-MS/MS, iv)publishing results, v)collaboration in a multinational environment and vi) reporting are helpful, as well as vii)interactions with wastewater treatment plants. Some of these can be developed during the project.

Who we are

Most scientific information on the group is available under https://projects.au.dk/waterpurification//
The group has own ozonation and biofilm reactors as well as two triple quad HPLC-MS/MS systems, two HPLC-MS/MS systems with high resolution and one imaging mass spectrometer. 

Place of work and area of employment 

Aarhus University, Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde 

Contact information

Interested candidates are welcome to contact: Prof. Kai Bester (kb@envs.au.dk or +4593508089) 

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than January 4, 2027. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

GREAT WORKSHOP • COMPETITIVE PAY • RELOCATION SUPPORT FOR YOU AND YOUR FAMILY
Are you an experienced machinist or industrial technician looking for a new opportunity abroad? At Service Shoppen, we are looking for a skilled and motivated colleague who enjoys precision engineering, turning and varied workshop tasks. Would you like to work in Denmark, enjoy a good work-life balance and become part of a friendly and professional workshop team? We would love to hear from you!

A NEW JOB – AND SUPPORT WITH YOUR MOVE TO DENMARK
Moving to another country is a big step, especially if you are bringing your family. We will help you get settled in Denmark – from airport pick-up and temporary accommodation to finding a permanent home and getting started with Danish language classes. If you wish to bring your family, we will also help you get started with the practical arrangements. Denmark offers good educational opportunities, schools and plenty of leisure activities for children and adults.

THE JOB
Your main responsibility will be NC turning, including working with our Weiler lathes, which can be operated both manually and through NC control. You will also take part in other varied workshop and production tasks.

 Set up, program and operate NC lathes.
 Perform manual turning when required.
 Read and understand technical drawings.
 Ensure high quality and precision in your work.
 Contribute to varied workshop tasks and suggest improvements.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

 You are a qualified Industrial Technician / Machinist or have relevant professional experience.
 You have experience with NC turning or CNC turning.
 You can work independently, take responsibility and take pride in quality work.
 You enjoy variety, teamwork and developing your skills.
 You can communicate in English. Danish is not required when you start.
 A valid EU passport is a requirement for this position.

YOUR RELOCATION TO DENMARK – WE WILL HELP

AIRPORT PICK-UP
We will pick you up at the airport and take you to your accommodation when you arrive.
TEMPORARY ACCOMMODATION
If needed, we will help arrange an apartment, a room or temporary bed & breakfast accommodation while you look for a permanent home.
FINDING A HOME
We will assist you in finding suitable permanent accommodation in Denmark.
DANISH LANGUAGE SCHOOL & PRACTICAL HELP
We will help you get started with Danish language classes and guide you through practical matters related to settling in Denmark.

PERSONAL CONTACT: Both of our managers speak English, and one of them is also fluent in Spanish. You will have someone to communicate with throughout the process and someone to turn to if you have questions.

WHAT WE OFFER

• DKK 205 per hour
• 37 hours per week
• 5 weeks + 1 additional week of holiday

You will also receive:

 An additional 10% of your salary through our free-choice scheme (fritvalgsordning), paid out twice a year.
 Employment conditions are covered by the DI/CO collective agreement, ensuring fair pay and proper working conditions.
 A flexible working environment.
 Thorough training and a proper introduction to your new job.
 Varied and interesting workshop tasks.
 A friendly and informal workshop with a strong professional focus.
Holiday: 5 weeks of annual holiday plus 1 additional week of holiday days. Public holidays are also days off.

ABOUT SERVICE SHOPPEN
At Service Shoppen, you will become part of a professional workshop environment where precision, quality and practical skills are important. We offer varied tasks and a friendly, informal atmosphere, where colleagues work together and take pride in delivering good workmanship. You will have the opportunity to use your professional skills, learn new things and become an important part of our team.

INTERESTED? LET’S TALK!
You do not need to live in Denmark to apply. We are happy to arrange an initial online conversation to get to know you and answer your questions about the job, Service Shoppen and moving to Denmark.
Send your CV and a short introduction to:
Email: mail@service-shoppen.com Phone: +45 55 77 21 58
Website: https://service-shoppen.com/

TÉCNICO INDUSTRIAL / TORNERO
¡Trabaja en Dinamarca! Buen salario y ayuda con la mudanza para ti y tu familia.

En Service Shoppen buscamos un técnico industrial o tornero con experiencia para formar parte de nuestro equipo en Næstved, Dinamarca. El trabajo consiste principalmente en torneado NC, utilizando tornos Weiler que pueden manejarse tanto manualmente como mediante control NC. Te ofrecemos ayuda con la recogida en el aeropuerto, alojamiento temporal, búsqueda de vivienda, clases de danés y los trámites prácticos para instalarte en Dinamarca. ¿Quieres trasladarte con tu familia? Are you passionate about designing and improving global business processes?

Do you want to play a key role in enabling transformation by bringing deep domain expertise and driving process excellence?

Ambu is transforming – and this is your opportunity to drive that transformation at scale.

We are strengthening our global process organisation and are building a Global Process Lead (GPL) layer across a range of end-to-end business processes spanning the full value chain—from planning and operations to finance, compliance, and product lifecycle management.

As part of this transformation, we are maturing our global processes, governance structures, and ways of working to support a more scalable and standardised operating model.

A key element of this journey is the implementation and rollout of core enterprise systems such as ERP, QMS, and PLM, enabling improved process consistency and integration across the organisation.

The role

As a Global Process Lead, you support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Ambu’s product design process. This includes mechanical design, electrical design, manufacturing process design and managing engineering data across these subprocesses and across our IT systems, primarily our PLM. Specific subprocesses within the PLM include creation of EBOM, translation of EBOM to MBOM and product master data management.

You play a key role in translating business needs into robust, scalable processes aligned with global standards.

Working closely with the Global Process Owners, Subject Matter Experts, technical workstream leads, and stakeholders across functions and geographical sites, you will contribute to process design, support implementation, and help ensure adoption of new ways of working.

This is a high-impact role where functional expertise meets cross-functional collaboration, and where you actively contribute to driving process excellence across Ambu.

Key Responsibilities

****Process design and domain expertise (primary focus)

**

• Ensure the design process integrates into the global product development process

• Provide deep functional expertise and ensure high-quality process documentation and standards

• Contribute to defining future-state processes and capabilities that allow our engineers to design products effectively, efficiently and in compliance with regulatory requirements.

• Establish and maintain Standard Operating Procedures for the Design Processes that setup our engineers for success.

**Continuous improvement and execution support

**

• Identify and drive improvements that improve the product, reduce time to market and ensure regulatory compliance.

• Support implementation of process changes and ensure adoption across regions and sites

• Facilitate workshops and collaboration across functions to refine and improve processes

• Contribute to building a culture of continuous improvement

**Stakeholder collaboration

**

• Work closely with stakeholders across functions, regions, and sites to ensure alignment

• Support communication and anchoring of process changes in the organisation

• Act as a key contributor in transformation initiatives and projects

• Ensure effective collaboration between global and local teams

**Suggested candidate profile

**You are likely to succeed in this role if you:

• Relevant experience from industry or consulting, working within PLM-powered product design

• A strong combination of functional domain expertise and an interest in process design and improvement

• Experience from a similar or related role in an industrial or global organization is preferred, especially from within the medical device industry

• Solid experience working with cross-functional processes and stakeholders in a global context

• Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills, with attention to detail in process design and documentation

• A collaborative mindset with the ability to engage stakeholders and support alignment across functions and regions

• A proactive and solution-oriented approach, with a continuous improvement mindset

• Willingness to travel regularly as part of a global role, supporting collaboration and implementation across Ambu’s footprint (including the US, Malaysia, China, and Mexico)

• Comfortable working across time zones, with flexibility to occasionally engage outside standard working hours

• Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company experiencing rapid growth with ambitious targets. We achieve this through collaboration between highly skilled and motivated employees. Your contributions will be central to our success, and you will join an international environment with strong opportunities for professional and personal development.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy (IFA), Aarhus University, Denmark (www.phys.au.dk) invites applications for a 2-year research assistant position with focus on establishing and maintaining trapped ion quantum technology setups. The work will partly be carried out in the newly established Quantum Tech-nology Lab (QTL) and within the Ion Trap Group.

The position is open from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Your profile
The candidates are expected to have experience in cold trapped ion research, and hence both have experience in ion trap and laser technology. We are seeking enthusiastic candidates with a keen interest in setting up a new teaching ion trap setup in QTL as well as participate in maintaining and running ion trap experiments within the Ion Trap Group. More specifically, the candidate should have a solid background in construction and operating rf ion traps, CW laser systems including control of output powers, polarization states, linewidths and frequencies, as well as an understanding of analog and digital electronics for experimental control. Relevant methodology includes UHV vacuum handling, rf circuity electronics, laser frequency stabilization using optical frequency combs, rubidium atomic clocks, and GPS synchronization.

Applicants must be able to document relevant experience, as outlined above.

Who we are / The department
The Department of Physics and Astronomy is a department at the Faculty of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark. The main objectives of the Department are to carry out research at the highest interna-tional level, to offer research based teaching at Bachelor of Science, Master of Science and PhD levels, and to exchange knowledge with other areas of society, e.g. by offering our expertise to industrial partners and the business world.

The Department is an attractive workplace for researchers, teachers, technicians, laboratory technicians and administrators and has a good study environment with many talented and active students at all levels. The research at the Department of Physics and Astronomy is of high quality, attracts significant international attention – in several fields the Department is within the world elite – and is characterized by many international collaborations with other high-ranking universities and research institutions around the world.

The place of work is Ny Munkegade 120, 8000 Aarhus C and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

The successful candidate is offered
• a working climate inviting lively, open and constructive discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
• a job where the overall environment in Denmark is family-friendly, safe and relaxed – contributing to Denmark consistently being voted amongst the happiest nations in the world.
 
Job description
Your tasks include:

• Establishing and running a novel linear rf ion trap setup for teaching purposes
• Handling existing CW laser systems including commercial external cavity diode laser systems, TiSa-lasers, fiber-lasers for trapped ion experiments
• Handling (electro-)optical setups for controlling the frequency and shaping the power level of CW laser
• Help developing experimental control systems based on the platform ARTIQ (ARTIQ)

Contact information
Further information can be obtained from Michael Drewsen (drewsen@phys.au.dk)

Deadline
The application deadline is 13 December 2026. 

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. People & Organization
